newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi jumps on technical trade, seen cheap.
newsitem.headline: Sappi jumps on technical trade, seen cheap.

text.p: Shares in South African paper and pulp producer Sappi Ltd bounded higher in brisk trading on Wednesday, taking its gains since the beginning of the year to almost 10 percent.
Traders on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said there was no fundamental reason for the stock's strong run, but that it had broken a key charting level on the upside and predicted further strength.
"The chartists say 42 rand was a resistance level. It broke through that on the upside and they are now talking of it going to 49 or 50 rand," one dealer said.
Sappi leapt five percent to a best level of 46.20 rand on Wednesday -- its highest level in five months. It touched a year low of 39.25 rand in November.
Other traders said gains, which were most marked on Tuesday and Wednesday, came on the back of strength throughout the industrial market.
"Sappi was oversold and it is now going up with the rest of the market...There is a bit of room for it to go up especially if world markets continue higher," a trader said.

By 0930 GMT stocks had slipped off their highs to trade at 46.10, a rise of 4.78 percent, after 272,900 shares worth over 1.25 million rand had traded mainly at the hands of institutions, dealers said.

In December Sappi reported earnings for the year to end September down a massive 73 percent to 230 cents a share mainly due to soft world pulp and paper demand and prices, and following losses on rand forward exchange contracts.
The firm predicted stronger export earnings in the new financial year on the back of the weaker rand and said its entire forward exchange burden had been cleared.
